sections.title: Pendahuluan dan Definisi

content.text: Movement disorders are neurological symptoms presenting as disturbances of voluntary movement and postural dysfunction. These are not caused by weakness due to abnormal muscle tone. The clinical picture is highly complex, variable, and sometimes unusual. Diagnosis can be challenging but is achievable through careful clinical examination.

sections.title: Penyakit Parkinson

content.text: Parkinson disease is a form of parkinsonism characterized by degeneration of the substantia nigra pars compacta. Parkinsonism is a syndrome marked by resting tremor, rigidity, bradikinesia, and loss of postural reflexes due to dopamine deficiency.

The four cardinal symptoms (TRAP) are: Tremor, Rigiditas, Akinesia/Bradikinesia, and Postural reflex impairment. Items 1-3 are called the three cardinal signs. Presentation may be unilateral or bilateral, symmetric or asymmetric.
Gejala kardinal: Tremor, Rigiditas, Akinesia/Bradikinesia, Postural reflex berkurang
Klasifikasi: Parkinsonisme idiopatik (primer), simptomatik (sekunder), Parkinson plus (multiple system degeneration), Heredodegeneratif
Postural instability typically appears in Hoehn-Yahr stage III and beyond; it is a late feature, not an early sign

sections.title: Terapi Farmakologis PD

content.text: Pharmacological therapy is tailored to patient age, disease stage, side effect profile, and cost considerations. Long-term L-dopa use causes motor complications.
Long-term L-dopa causes motoric complications; younger patients may benefit from starting with DA agonists

sections.title: Komplikasi Non-Motorik dan Motorik PD

content.text: NON-MOTOR COMPLICATIONS: Neuropsychiatric - depression (TCAs, SSRIs, pramipexole), psychosis (reduce dopaminergic therapy, avoid polypharmacy), anxiety, cognitive impairment/dementia (rivastigmine, cholinesterase inhibitors). Autonomic - orthostatic hypotension (fluids, elastic stockings, ephedrine 15-45mg/day, fludrocortisone 100-300mcg/day, midodrine 2.5-10mg/day), GI dysfunction (dysphagia, constipation, sialorrhea), urinary dysfunction (oxybutynin, desmopressin), sexual dysfunction. Sensory - pain (optimize dopaminergic therapy, botox), hyposmia. Sleep - insomnia, excessive daytime sleepiness.

MOTOR COMPLICATIONS: Fluctuations - wearing off (short L-dopa effect), on-off phenomena. Dyskinesia - ballismus, dystonia. Management includes L-dopa dose adjustment, COMT inhibitors (entacapone) + L-dopa, pramipexole, ropinirole.
Motor fluctuations and dyskinesias are hallmarks of advanced PD and long-term L-dopa therapy

sections.title: Parkinsonisme Sekunder dan MSA

content.text: Secondary parkinsonism resembles PD but has known causes including drug exposure, toxins, or structural lesions. Management includes removing the causative agent. Parkinson-plus syndromes include corticobasal degeneration, dementia syndromes, multiple system atrophy (MSA), and progressive supranuclear palsy.

MSA is a degenerative disease resembling parkinsonism with cerebellar signs and autonomic dysfunction. MSA-P (parkinsonism-dominant): incontinence, erectile dysfunction. MSA-C (cerebellar-dominant): nystagmus, dysarthria, ataxia. Red flags (MSA features): postural instability, orofacial dystonia, incontinence, myoclonic tremor, stridor and sigh inspiration, pyramidal signs. Probable MSA: age >30, urinary incontinence + orthostatic hypotension, responds to levodopa.
MSA-P (dominan parkinsonism): inkontinensia, disfungsi ereksi
MSA-C (dominan tanda serebelar): nistagmus, disartria, ataksia
Terapi: Levodopa untuk parkinsonism; hipotensi ortostatik (head up tilt, diet tinggi garam, elastic stocking, efedrin, fludrocortison, midodrine)
Disfungsi urinary: Oxybutynin dan Desmopresin spray

sections.title: Tremor dan Distonia

content.text: Tremor is defined as rhythmic oscillatory movement from alternating agonist-antagonist muscle contraction. Classification includes resting tremor, action tremor (postural, kinetic, intentional, simple kinetic). Essential tremor is bilateral, affects hands and head, onset in second decade, usually starts unilateral then becomes bilateral.

Tremor treatment: propranolol 60-80mg/day (start 30mg), primidone 62.5-300mg/day, gabapentin 900-1800mg/day, clozapine 12.5-50mg/day, clonazepam 0.5-6mg/day. Cerebellar tremor is typically difficult to treat (carbamazepine, clonazepam, ondansetron may help).

Dystonia shows hypotonia with alternating muscle spasms, twisted postures, and potential body deformity. Classified as primary (idiopathic), secondary, and dystonia-plus. Treatment: levodopa, dopamine agonists, anticholinergics. Botulinum toxin injection 40-400 units for focal dystonias. Blepharospasm (M:F = 1:3) treated with botulinum toxin. Writer's cramp: involuntary finger contractions treated with physiotherapy and trihexyphenidyl.
Tremor esensial: bilateral tangan dan kepala, onset dekade kedua
Propranolol 60-80mg/hari (dimulai 30mg/hari)
Distonia: levodopa, agonis dopamin, antikolinergik, toksin botulinum

sections.title: Tics, RLS, PLMD, dan Spasme Hemifasial

content.text: Tics are unconscious, brief, frequent, repetitive movements or sounds. Classification: Tourette syndrome (motor + vocal tics), chronic motor or vocal tic disorder, transient tic disorder (>4 weeks). Etiology involves biochemical imbalance in basal ganglia. Diagnosis uses MRI and EEG to rule out structural lesions. Treatment: non-neuroleptics (fluoxetine, paroxetine, clonidine) and neuroleptics (haloperidol, risperidone, clozapine).

Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) is a sensory-motor phenomenon with urge to move legs and unpleasant sensations. Classified as primary (genetic) or secondary (iron deficiency). By symptom pattern: intermittent, daily, or refractory. Clinical features: urge to move legs, worse in evening/night, causes sleep disruption, depression, usually family history, responds to dopaminergic therapy. Treatment goals: symptom reduction and secondary cause treatment. Non-pharmacological: mental activity, physical activity, sleep hygiene. Pharmacological: levodopa, dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole, pergolide), anticonvulsants, opioids for refractory cases.

Periodic Limb Movement Disorder (PLMD) involves repetitive leg jerks during sleep every ~40 seconds, 0.5-5 seconds in duration, occurring every 20-40 seconds. Diagnosed by overnight polysomnography. Treatment: benzodiazepines (clonazepam), dopaminergics (pramipexole), anticonvulsants, GABA agonists (baclofen).

Hemifacial spasm involves unilateral tonic or clonic contractions of facial muscles innervated by the facial nerve (CN VII). Treatment aims to reduce muscle contraction: carbamazepine, benzodiazepines, baclofen, gabapentin, botulinum toxin injection, or surgery.
Tourette syndrome: kombinasi tics motorik dan vokal
RLS: agonis dopamin (pramipexol, ropinirol, pergalide), levodopa, antikonvulsan, opioid
PLMD: klonazepam, pramipexole, antikonvulsan, baklofen
Spasme hemifasial: karbamazepin, benzodiazepin, baklofen, gabapentin, toksin botulinum, pembedahan

diagnostic_logic.title: Identify if movement disorder is present
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Distinguish from weakness, spasticity, or other motor deficits

diagnostic_logic.title: Classify as hyperkinetic or hypokinetic
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Hyperkinetic = excessive movement (tremor, chorea, dystonia); Hypokinetic = reduced movement (PD, bradykinesia)

diagnostic_logic.title: Localize to anatomical structure
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Substantia nigra = PD; subthalamic nucleus = ballism; caudate = chorea; putamen = dystonia

diagnostic_logic.title: Apply specific diagnostic criteria
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Hughes criteria for PD; clinical features for tremor classification

differential_notes.how_to_separate: Essential tremor: action tremor, bilateral, head involvement; PD tremor: resting tremor, pill-rolling, unilateral onset
Secondary dystonia has identifiable cause (drug, structural lesion); primary has no identified cause
MSA-P has early autonomic dysfunction, poor levodopa response, cerebellar signs

treatment_notes.content: L-dopa or DA agonist for age 40-60
L-dopa first-line for age >60, add DA agonist later
COMT inhibitors (entacapone), DA agonists, adjust L-dopa timing
Propranolol, primidone, gabapentin; botulinum toxin for dystonic tremor
Levodopa trial, anticholinergics, botulinum toxin injection
Dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole), levodopa, anticonvulsants, iron replacement if deficient

red_flags: Early postural instability (suggests MSA or PSP, not idiopathic PD)
Rapid progression with poor levodopa response
Early autonomic failure (urinary incontinence, orthostatic hypotension)
Pyramidal signs or cerebellar ataxia with parkinsonism
